# weather.client.WeatherService { #spotforecast2_safe.weather.client.WeatherService }

```python
weather.client.WeatherService(
    latitude,
    longitude,
    cache_path=None,
    use_forecast=True,
)
```

High-level service for weather data generation.

Extends WeatherClient with caching, hybrid fetching (archive+forecast),
and fallback strategies.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                       | Default    |
|--------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| latitude     | [float](`float`)               | Latitude of the location.                                                                                                                                                                         | _required_ |
| longitude    | [float](`float`)               | Longitude of the location.                                                                                                                                                                        | _required_ |
| cache_path   | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| None | Optional path to cache file for storing fetched data. If provided, the service will attempt to load from cache before fetching and will save new data to this path. Default is None (no caching). | `None`     |
| use_forecast | [bool](`bool`)                 | Whether to use forecast data for future dates (default True).                                                                                                                                     | `True`     |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.weather import WeatherService
client = WeatherService(latitude=52.52, longitude=13.405, cache_path=Path("weather_cache.parquet"))
start = pd.Timestamp("2023-01-01", tz="UTC")
end = pd.Timestamp("2023-01-07", tz="UTC")
df = client.get_dataframe(start=start, end=end, fill_missing=False)
print(df.head())
print(df.tail())
```

### get_dataframe { #spotforecast2_safe.weather.client.WeatherService.get_dataframe }

```python
weather.client.WeatherService.get_dataframe(
    start,
    end,
    timezone='UTC',
    freq='h',
    fallback_on_failure=True,
    fill_missing=False,
)
```

Get weather DataFrame for a specified range using best available methods.

Refactored from spotpredict.create_weather_df.  Since the 1.0
major release, remaining gaps after fetch are **rejected** by
default so that synthesised values never reach downstream
consumers labelled as measurements.  Pass ``fill_missing=True``
to opt into the legacy forward/back-fill behavior.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                | Type                                                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      | Default    |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| start               | [str](`str`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Start date for the data.                                                                                                                                                                         | _required_ |
| end                 | [str](`str`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | End date for the data.                                                                                                                                                                           | _required_ |
| timezone            | [str](`str`)                                                   | Timezone for the data (default "UTC").                                                                                                                                                           | `'UTC'`    |
| freq                | [str](`str`)                                                   | Frequency for the data (default "h").                                                                                                                                                            | `'h'`      |
| fallback_on_failure | [bool](`bool`)                                                 | Whether to use fallback data on failure (default True).                                                                                                                                          | `True`     |
| fill_missing        | [bool](`bool`)                                                 | Whether to forward- and back-fill remaining NaN gaps after fetch/resample (default False).  When False (the fail-safe default), any remaining NaN raises ``ValueError`` with the gap timestamps. | `False`    |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If ``fill_missing=False`` and the merged frame still contains NaNs after resample. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.weather import WeatherService
client = WeatherService(latitude=51.0267, longitude=7.5693)
# get the weather data for the last week, using the cache if available, and filling any remaining gaps
start = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC") - pd.Timedelta(days=7)
end = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC")
df = client.get_dataframe(start=start, end=end, fill_missing=False)
print(df.head())
print(df.tail())
```
